title: Focaccia a la Ashley
description: Ashley made this for our 2022 Family Reunion in Myrtle Beach and then again (twice!) on a long Penn State football weekend later in the Fall. What a treat every time! Take a picture for Ashley if you make it.
ingredients: 1 heaping tsp active dry yeast (instant is fine too)
2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, plus additional for kneading
1 cup extra virgin olive oil, divided
2 TB rosemary or herbs of your choice (optional)
directions: Combine warm water, yeast, and sugar in a mixing bowl. Swish with your hand (like a bathtub) until combined. Cover and leave until yeast is bubbling and aromatic - at least 5 mins.

Add flour, then salt, and 1/2 cup olive oil to the yeast mixture, and stir with your hand to combine. Optional herbs can also be added at this time. You can also do this in a stand mixer with a dough hook if you prefer. Once the dough has come together, turn it out on a floured kitchen counter and knead for 3-5 minutes until the dough becomes smooth and soft. Give it a sprinkle of flour if the dough is really sticky/tacky. (Be careful of adding too much flour as focaccia dough should be on the wetter side)

Coat the inside of your bowl with olive oil, and return the dough to the bowl. Cover it with plastic wrap and put it in a warm place (like the laundry room with the dryer on!) until it is doubled in size, at least one hour.

Coat a 9x13 baking dish with the remaining 1/2 cup of olive oil. (This may seem excessive, but focaccia is an oily crusted bread and that is why it's so delicious.) Note: you can also use 2 cast iron pans or two 9 inch pie pans instead of the baking dish if that's what you have.

Carefully put the dough in the pan, and begin pressing it out with your fingers to fit the size of the pan. (Try to maintain all of the air in the dough- do not "punch down" the dough). Turn the dough over to coat the other side with the olive oil. Continue to gently stretch the dough to fit the pan. (If it's proving difficult to stretch, wait 5 minutes and revisit). As you are stretching the dough, spread your fingers out and make finger holes all the way through the dough, piercing it. (Yes, this is strange! But when the dough rises again it will create the characteristic craggy-looking focaccia. If you do not make the actual holes in the dough, the finished product will be very smooth.)
Cover the pan with plastic wrap and put it back in a warm place until it has doubled in size, about 1 hour. Towards the end of the rising time, preheat the oven to 425 degrees F.

Liberally sprinkle the top of the focaccia with Maldon salt flakes and lightly drizzle a little oil on top if it seems dry. Bake until the top is golden brown (about 20-25 mins). Remove the focaccia from the oven and let it cool slightly before cutting and serving. Focaccia is always best served warm out of the oven!
notes:
Notes:
This is a very forgiving recipe - I have experimented with more and less olive oil and it generally turns out well either way. I've also used 1/2 bread flour and 1/2 AP and it's still good. I've also rushed the second rise and while not as puffy, it is still very good!
If you'd like additional toppings, press onto the top of the dough before the 2nd rise. I recommend any kind of tender herbs, grape tomatoes, cloves of garlic, olives, parm cheese or anything you love!
